company.name: Willis Towers Watson Public Limited Company - Ordinary Shares
company.display_name: Willis Towers Watson Public Limited Company - Ordinary Shares

special_handling: Fiduciary assets and matching fiduciary liabilities are client money and excluded from detachable cash.
analysis_model.reason: WTW earns commissions and fees from insurance broking, consulting, administration and technology; it does not underwrite insurance risk. The operating company model applies, while matched client fiduciary balances require exclusion.

assets.explanation: Year-end corporate cash; only 50% is credited in earnback because part is regulated capital, working liquidity, or earmarked for the January 2026 Newfront acquisition.
Cash and receivables held for insurance-broking clients, exactly matched by fiduciary liabilities; not company surplus cash.
Fees and commissions receivable from a diversified client base; operating working capital, not detachable.
Goodwill plus other intangibles, mainly acquired client relationships and franchises; supports earnings but is not liquidation cash.

liabilities.explanation: Amounts owed to insurers and clients against fiduciary assets; pass-through operating balances.
Current and long-term debt, including $1.0bn notes issued late in 2025 ahead of acquisitions; deducted in full from detachable cash.
Client prepayments and accrued operating expenses tied to service delivery and compensation; not treated as financing debt.

owner_earnback.interpretation: At the input market value, WTW is net-debt funded after excluding client fiduciary money. Crediting only half of year-end cash and applying a 10% haircut to 2025 free cash flow gives about 24.9 years to recover the enterprise purchase price. This is a conservative owner-earnback estimate, not a forecast or target price.

cash_breakdown.reason: Half credit for regulated capital, working liquidity and acquisition earmarking.
Client fiduciary assets and liabilities match and are excluded.

profit_adjustments.reason: Operating cash flow less fixed-asset and software additions.
10% buffer for working-capital variability, professional liability and integration execution.

dividend.forecast_basis: Annualized $0.96 quarterly dividend approved in February 2026, multiplied by 94,545,903 shares outstanding at 2026-02-20 and translated at CNY7.0358/USD.

history.basis: $358m cash dividends paid in 2025, translated at CNY7.0358/USD.
$354m cash dividends paid in 2024, translated at CNY7.0358/USD.

business.one_line: WTW向全球企业和机构收取保险经纪佣金及人力资本、福利、投资与风险咨询服务费。
business.main_business: Two integrated segments: Health, Wealth & Career provides employee-benefit, retirement, investment, compensation and outsourcing advice/technology; Risk & Broking provides corporate insurance broking, risk advice and insurance consulting technology.
business.profit_source: Recurring commissions linked to insurance premiums and professional fees for consulting and administration. HWC contributed 55% of 2025 segment revenue and $1.681bn segment operating income; R&B contributed 45% and $1.072bn.
business.business_model: Asset-light, people- and relationship-intensive intermediary/advisory model serving diversified corporate and institutional clients in more than 140 countries. Revenue depends on adviser talent, client retention, insurance premium levels and project demand; capital expenditure is modest relative to revenue.
business.industry_position: A leading global advisory, broking and solutions firm with about 47,000 employees. Scale, global placement capabilities, data and long client relationships matter; no single client is material, but competition for talent and large accounts is persistent.

risks.impact: Broking and consulting errors can create long-tail provisions and cash losses; the 10-K identifies E&O provision estimation as a critical audit matter.

The $1.0bn late-2025 debt issuance and $775m January 2026 delayed-draw facility relate to acquisitions, so year-end cash overstates freely distributable liquidity relative to the August 2026 valuation date.
Salaries were 58% of revenue; weak retention or wage pressure can compress margins, while brokerage commissions vary with premium levels.
Goodwill and intangibles equal roughly CNY70.9bn; the 2024 TRANZACT disposal involved a $1.0bn goodwill impairment, showing acquisition values can be revised sharply.

evidence.claim: 2025 audited financial statements and business model
FY2025 adjusted results, organic growth and free cash flow
2026 quarterly dividend of $0.96 and historical payments
USD/CNY conversion rate 7.0358 used as a near-year-end translation proxy
Market capitalization CNY210.52bn at 2026-08-03 and PE TTM 20.78713

limitations: All USD financial statements are translated at CNY7.0358/USD, the nearest directly verified PBOC year-end central parity found (2025-12-26), rather than transaction-specific rates.
Gross profit is an analytical proxy: revenue less salaries and benefits and other operating expenses; WTW does not report a GAAP gross-profit subtotal.
The market capitalization date is seven months after the balance-sheet date and follows the Newfront acquisition; earnback discounts year-end cash to reduce this timing mismatch.
